case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed summary judgment for hospital staff who reported suspected physical abuse, placed a 72-hour hold on the child, and photographed and examined her without parental consent, holding they acted in subjective good faith under KRS 620.050(1) and that the KRS 620.050(14) negligence exception reaches only negligently performed diagnostics, not the decision to perform them.
key_cases.relevance: It construes KRS 620.050(14), the statute authorizing photographs, X-rays, and other diagnostic procedures on a child without parental consent as part of an abuse evaluation.
key_cases.quote: We believe the negligence exception is intended to apply only where the diagnostics are administered negligently in some way so as to cause injury to the patient

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed governmental immunity for the University of Kentucky Medical Center and held that the newborn's attending physician was immune under KRS 620.050(1) for the reporting of a mislabeled meconium drug screen that led to the infant's removal, because she acted in good faith and neither the KRS 620.050(2) Cabinet-employee exception nor the subsection (14) negligent-diagnostics exception applied.
key_cases.relevance: This is the first Kentucky construction of the KRS 620.050(14) negligence exception, held inapplicable because the diagnostic test was performed before the abuse report rather than at the Cabinet's request following one.
key_cases.quote: having concluded that Dr. Leahy-Auer has immunity from liability under KRS 620.030(1) and KRS 620.050(1), any error which may have occurred at the trial of this action is moot
